raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates complete opacification (white-out) of the left hemithorax with a contralateral mediastinal shift to the right, which is the classic radiographic appearance of a massive pleural effusion pushing structures away from the affected side. In contrast, lung collapse would cause an ipsilateral shift toward the opacity, and pneumothorax would appear radiolucent (black) rather than opaque.
